title: URL state serialisation preserves sort, filter and page across reload and share
asA: operator sharing a specific datatable view with a colleague
iWant: the sort, filter and page state to serialise into the URL so a reload or a shared link lands on the same view
soThat: the surface is deep-linkable and reload-stable (ADR-1802's recommended default)

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a rendered datatable where the operator applied a sort, a filter and advanced past page 1, the current URL carries the state as query parameters (`sort`, `q`, `page`) per ADR-1802's recommended default; reloading the URL rerenders the same view.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a rendered datatable with an applied sort, filter and non-first page
acceptanceCriteria.then: the reloaded surface renders the same sort, filter and page

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given the elicited client-side query adapter mode (`query-adapter-mode=client-side` per `blueprint.json:elicits[query-adapter-mode]`) applied to a small in-memory collection, the sort direction still writes to the URL so reload stability is preserved; the client-side branch never invents a URL state divergent from the server-side default. Applying agent sets: the elicited value on `blueprint.json:elicits[query-adapter-mode]` (`server-side` or `client-side`). The URL `sort=<column>:<asc|desc>` grammar is fixed on TAC-1802-application-datatable-query-adapter.responsibilities[0].
acceptanceCriteria.given: a rendered datatable applying the client-side sort alternative
acceptanceCriteria.when: the operator activates a sort control
acceptanceCriteria.then: the URL query parameters update with `sort=<column>:<direction>` in the same shape as the server-side default

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a rendered datatable, the default page size on the recommended default (ADR-1803) applies when no `pageSize` is present in the URL; the operator's elicited page-size override at apply time changes the default without changing the URL contract. Applying agent sets: the applied default page size from ADR-1803-application-datatable-page-size (25 unless the operator elicits an override on `blueprint.json:elicits[page-size]`). The query parameter name `pageSize` is fixed on TAC-1802-application-datatable-query-adapter.responsibilities[0].
acceptanceCriteria.given: a rendered datatable landed at the shell route without a `pageSize` query parameter
acceptanceCriteria.when: the initial render fetches the first page
acceptanceCriteria.then: the fetch carries `pageSize=<applied-default>` and the URL is left untouched

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given the elicited session-scoped alternative (`url-state-strategy=session-scoped` per ADR-1802), when the operator applies a sort, filter and page advance, the URL does NOT change (no query parameters appear) and the state is retained in memory for the shell mount lifetime; a reload of the URL lands on the default state (no state restoration) and the shell announces the session-scoped mode in the accessible copy on first mount.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an operator applying sort, filter and page under url-state-strategy=session-scoped
acceptanceCriteria.when: the pack inspects URL and state after operator actions
acceptanceCriteria.then: the URL carries no query parameters, the state is retained in memory for the mount lifetime, and reload lands on the default state

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a URL carrying an INVALID state (a `sort=notacolumn` referencing a column that does not exist on the schema, a `page=999` past the last page, a `q=<value>` longer than the input's maxlength), when the shell loads, the shell rejects the invalid parts of the URL state, falls back to the default for each rejected part, and announces the fallback through the aria-live polite region; a shell that hard-fails on invalid URL state fails the pack check.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a URL with invalid sort, page or q parameters
acceptanceCriteria.when: the shell mounts and reads the URL state
acceptanceCriteria.then: the shell rejects invalid parts, falls back to defaults per part, and announces the fallback; a hard failure on invalid URL state fails

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a rendered datatable, when the operator applies a new sort mid-view, the URL is updated with `history.replaceState` (not `pushState`); the browser history does NOT gain a new entry per micro-change so the operator's back button returns them to the page BEFORE the datatable, not to the previous sort state. A shell using `pushState` per micro-change fails the pack check per ADR-1802.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a rendered datatable and an operator applying a new sort
acceptanceCriteria.when: the pack inspects browser history after the sort
acceptanceCriteria.then: the URL updated via history.replaceState and no new history entry was added; pushState per micro-change fails per ADR-1802
